_comment: Severity qaydalari (28.10.2026): Acceptance Criteria Table 6 + Contract Exhibit 4 III/IV. tfs_value deyerleri TFS-de real defektlerde gorunub ('1 - Critical', '2 - High', '3 - Medium', '4 - Low'). Severity definition hele yekun deyil (tba) - deyisende yalniz bu fayli yenile.
required_note: Severity is needed only for PROD defects (Environment field contains PROD). Non-PROD defects may leave it empty.

severities.name: Critical
severities.label: Critical (Severity 1)
severities.summary: Process stopped / application down / major function broken; no workaround; data destroyed or at risk.
guidelines: Processes are stopped (e.g. the application is down or a major function is not working)
Application processes are stopped and the schedule impact will result in a severe delay to the software being deployed into production
Aztelekom cannot continue until the problem is resolved
Data is destroyed or at risk

sla.text: Reaction 1 h, resolution/workaround 7 h (with workaround: full fix within 10 calendar days), 24x7

severities.name: Major
severities.label: Major (Severity 2)
severities.summary: Significant partial malfunction; process severely degraded; a workaround exists only if it is resource-intensive.
guidelines: Application processes are severely degraded and the schedule impact will result in a severe delay to the Solution being deployed into production
Where a workaround is available it is resource intensive

sla.text: Reaction 3 h, resolution/workaround 24 h (with workaround: full fix within 15 calendar days), 24x7

severities.name: Medium
severities.label: Medium (Severity 3)
severities.summary: Works, but not to specification; an acceptable, cheap workaround exists.
guidelines: Process is operational but functions are not performing to specifications
Application processes are affected but the issue is not expected to affect the project's delivery into the production environment
An acceptable workaround is available and is not resource intensive

sla.text: Reaction 3 working days, resolution 15 working days, 8x5 (09:00-18:00 Baku, Mon-Fri)

severities.name: Low
severities.label: Low (Severity 4)
severities.summary: Cosmetic / non-functional: alignment, colour, spelling, documentation, help. Sev5 (question) is also logged as 4.
guidelines: The problem is cosmetic in nature
Examples: functionality not impacted, e.g. button alignment, color, grammar, spelling, report alignment, documentation, help

sla.text: Reaction 5 working days, resolution 30 working days, 8x5 (09:00-18:00 Baku, Mon-Fri)

severities.name: Enhancement
severities.label: Enhancement
severities.summary: New requirement -> change request, NOT a defect.
guidelines: A change required that is not in the current scope of the project; must be re-evaluated by the project team (new/additional user requirements)
Suggested enhancements which do not constitute a lack of required functionality
Should be raised as a change request, not as a defect

assessment_tests: One subscriber vs systematic: a problem on one subscriber/record pushes the severity down, a systematic problem (all subscribers / every run) pushes it up.
Wrong billing / payments or customer-facing impact pushes the severity up.
An acceptable, cheap workaround pushes the severity down; a resource-intensive workaround does not.
New requirement (not in scope / never specified) -> Enhancement / change request, not a defect.

sla_rules.clock_start: CreatedDate (registration triggers the SLA, contract IX)
sla_rules.reaction: first vendor comment or vendor state change
sla_rules.resolution_clock: time in vendor states (Proposed / New / Active / In Progress); paused while Resolved / Ready for Testing; open defects measured to now
sla_rules.working_hours: 09:00-18:00 Baku, Mon-Fri (holidays from config/holidays.json; empty -> holidays count as working days)
